items.title: George Justin Interview, 1958-06-01
items.q: I could remember another incident where I was working with a cousin of mine at the time. He was a saxophone player. His name was Dejean.

ctx.x: Did most of the fellas work at the post office?

Well I'd say about half of them, or maybe a little more than half, worked at the post office. Well I think that was a general idea to comprise a band with members of the post office. And well I got a big bang out of it for the simple reason. We'd rehearse twice a week and we'd have such a good time after the rehearsals. And that's the thing I always looked forward to was the food and drinks afterwards, you know. And it was the same condition. I guess I could have been a heck of a lot more advanced than I was if…

I haven't seen him in about three or four years since, of course I've been away from New Orleans for quite some time now since. When did you leave about? Well I left in 1936. I left there on the Steema Capitol. I was playing with Sidney Desveen at the time. And we played the boat for that summer. Went all the way up the river.
